History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
30-year-old male with 6-week history of left-sided hearing difficulty, intermittent tinnitus, and mild imbalance; plan is face-to-face otoscopic examination to rule out cerumen impaction or other ear pathology.

History:
• Primary complaint: Reduced hearing in left ear.  
• Onset/duration: Began ~6 weeks ago; prior brief episode one year ago resolved after a few days.  
• Course: Symptoms fluctuate; not constant.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Intermittent ringing (tinnitus) in left ear, triggered by television/music.  
  – Occasional mild dizziness/off-balance; no room-spinning vertigo; no associated nausea.  
• Pertinent negatives: No right-ear hearing loss, no ear pain, no otorrhea, no fever, no chest pain, no palpitations, no cotton-bud use.  
• Systems review beyond above: Not discussed.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Ringing provoked by certain sounds; no specific relievers noted.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions documented.  
• No past surgeries mentioned.  

Medications:
• None reported.

Allergies:
• Not documented.

Social History:
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drug use, occupation, and living situation not discussed.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• No in-consult physical exam performed.  
• Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
• None to date. Plan for otoscopic examination at in-person clinic visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss with tinnitus and mild dizziness  
  – Impression: Possible cerumen impaction or other external/middle ear pathology; differential includes inner-ear dysfunction contributing to tinnitus/dizziness.  
  – Plan:  
    • Schedule face-to-face GP appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination.  
    • If wax impaction found, remove as indicated; if ear canal/drum normal, pursue further evaluation for tinnitus/vestibular disorder.  
    • Provide patient with educational leaflet link on tinnitus for pre-visit reading.  
    • Patient to contact support team to arrange appointment; number left in notes.  
    • Advise patient to re-book video appointment sooner if symptoms worsen or new issues arise.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: allergies, regular medications, complete past medical history, social history, vitals.  
• Internal conflicts: None detected.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor gaps but did not affect clinical understanding.
